key_insight: The paper argues that AI safety needs new mathematics to make systems legible, steerable, and cooperative with humans, with different core problems mapped to different branches of math.
engineering_relevance: For AI engineers, this frames safety as a design and verification problem spanning cooperation, world-modeling, feature representation, and training stability rather than a single model-alignment technique.
method: Logic and game theory for cooperation
Algebra, representation theory, analysis, and geometry for learned features, generalization, and training dynamics
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a field-organized conceptual survey with accessible open problems, but does not report experiments, datasets, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: The ideas are high-level and mathematically broad, so practical impact depends on translating open-ended theory into testable AI safety methods.
paper_title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
